 Equinix Opens SG6 to Support Singapore's Digital Future and Strengthen Its Role as a Global Innovation Hub
 November 6, 2026 
 SHARE 
 Share this page on LinkedIn 
 Share this page on Facebook 
 Share this page on X 
 View File Download File 
 AI-ready and sustainability-focused data center enables businesses to connect, innovate and scale through a globally connected digital ecosystem 
 SINGAPORE, November 6, 2026 – Singapore's Digital Economy nominal value-added reached S$144.1 billion in 2025 (19.3% of GDP), up from S$136.5 billion (18.8% of GDP) in 2024, growing 5.6% year-on-year, faster than the 3.1% nominal GDP growth 1 . Today, Equinix, Inc. (Nasdaq: EQIX), the world’s digital infrastructure company ® , announced the opening of SG6, its sixth International Business Exchange (IBX) data center in Singapore, setting a global innovation and sustainability benchmark for the digital infrastructure industry to support the nation’s digital economy. The opening ceremony was graced by Mr. Tan Kiat How, Senior Minister of State, Ministry of Digital Development and Information .
 As the first facility in Equinix’s portfolio built under the Singapore Government's Data Centre – Call for Application (DC-CFA) process, SG6 is designed to reconcile the performance and density requirements of AI and data-intensive workloads with Singapore’s strict national sustainability mandates. This state-of-the-art facility brings together sustainably-designed, high-performance infrastructure, private interconnection, and global ecosystems of enterprises, cloud providers and technology partners, enabling businesses in Singapore to responsibly innovate, scale and connect to opportunities worldwide.
 SG6 represents Equinix’s commitment to helping Singapore realize its global digital ambitions while ensuring sustainability goes hand-in-hand with technological growth and innovation. Through its Future First sustainability strategy, Equinix is advancing ambitious environmental goals, including science-based net-zero emissions targets by 2040 and 100% global renewable energy coverage by 2030. Equinix is committed to being a responsible neighbor, working closely with the communities where it operates to ensure its facilities benefit the people who live and work around them. These commitments strongly support and complement the country’s broader sustainability and decarbonization agenda.
 SG6 operating temperatures will meet the ASHRAE A1A standard. It also features several energy-efficient innovations, including proprietary cooling array technology and liquid-cooling to support high-density AI deployments and power-intensive GPU infrastructure. In addition, SG6 incorporates onsite renewable energy generation through solar photovoltaic panels installed on the rooftop and the facade of the building, contributing to its 100% clean and renewable energy coverage. The facility, designed with Singapore’s Green DC Roadmap in mind, also boasts several other green building features such as efficient water management systems.
 In support of Singapore’s innovation ecosystem, SG6 will host a Co-Innovation Facility (CIF) in partnership with the National University of Singapore Energy Solutions Hub, targeted to open in 2027. The facility will advance data center sustainability and energy innovation by focusing on emerging technologies such as liquid cooling, cognitive digital twins, and battery energy storage. The CIF will provide a platform to test and scale new solutions that support Singapore’s digital and AI ambitions while enabling industry and academia to experiment with emerging use cases and translate innovative ideas into real-world applications.
 Equinix has operated in Singapore since 2002, has grown from one facility to six data centers in the country and remains committed to investing in the country’s people, partners and communities for the long term. Earlier in August 2026, Equinix was also announced as one of the four data center operators awarded capacity under the second DC-CFA.
 Highlights/Key Facts: 
 Equinix has the most network-dense data centers in Singapore that house many of the international and regional networks connecting South Asia as well as subsea connectivity to markets in every continent through more than 17 subsea cables. Equinix’s Singapore colocation facilities enable customers to be part of a rich industry ecosystem of financial services companies, cloud services, biomedical sciences, IT, communications, media, physical sciences and engineering industries.
 With an initial investment of US$290 million, SG6 will provide approximately 1,550 cabinets in Phase 1, and up to 20MW of IT capacity upon full build-out.
 SG6 is designed to achieve a Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.20 and is targeting BCA-IMDA Green Mark Platinum certification. It also incorporates sustainability features such as highly efficient cooling systems and lower-embodied-carbon construction materials.
 Aligned with SS 715:2025, Singapore's national standard for energy efficiency, customer IT server equipment deployed at SG6 must hold a recognized energy efficiency certification or demonstrate an equivalent level of efficiency.
 SG6 is designed to support sustainable water management through a range of innovative water conservation and reuse initiatives. The facility utilizes NEWater and rainwater harvesting systems to reduce reliance on potable water, collecting and storing rainwater for cooling tower operations.
 Equinix data centers in Singapore have achieved 100% renewables coverage since 2020. Equinix has signed four renewable energy power purchase agreements in Singapore, expanding its local renewable energy portfolio to a cumulative 215MWp by 2028, reinforcing its position as one of the leading colocation off-takers in the nation.
 Globally, Equinix operates more than 280 data centers across 77 markets in 36 countries. In Asia-Pacific, Equinix operates 65 data centers across key metros in Australia, China 2 , Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, and Philippines.
 Supporting Quotes: 
 Adaire Fox-Martin, Chief Executive Officer and President, Equinix , said, “Singapore sits at the intersection of global commerce, digital technology and sustainable development. Equinix has been investing in Singapore for nearly 25 years, and our new facility will further expand our presence as the neutral exchange where enterprises connect to the clouds, networks and partners they need to innovate and grow. Singapore is one of our most important markets globally, and our continued investment here is a testament to the central role it plays in the digital economy.”
 Cyrus Adaggra, President, Asia-Pacific, Equinix, said, "Asia-Pacific is at the forefront of digital transformation, with AI adoption, cloud expansion and data-intensive workloads driving unprecedented demand for high-performance digital infrastructure. Singapore remains a strategic gateway for businesses serving the region, connecting key markets, talent and innovation ecosystems. SG6 strengthens our ability to support customers as they scale across Asia-Pacific, providing the resilient, interconnected and sustainable infrastructure they need to accelerate innovation and capture new growth opportunities."
 Yee May Leong, Managing Director, Singapore, Equinix , commented, "Singapore’s strength has always been its ability to look ahead — to embrace growth and innovation while being thoughtful about how we use our resources. As AI creates new opportunities and increases demand for digital infrastructure, I believe our next chapter must be about how we grow sustainably — supporting economic and digital growth while using our finite resources responsibly. SG6 reflects our commitment to this journey, providing the resilient, highly connected and sustainable infrastructure that will help Singapore remain a trusted global and regional hub. I’m proud that Equinix can continue to play a part in Singapore’s growth, working alongside government and industry to enable the next generation of AI and innovation, while building a more resilient and sustainable future.”
